static_traits.name: Liu Jing
static_traits.family_status: Lives in a rural house with her husband, who is a soldier, expecting their first child; her father is a missionary.
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends and a father to talk to when in difficulty, but she struggles to share her feelings of inadequacy with them; these feelings have affected her relationship with her husband.
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior counseling or treatment history; no similar psychological problems before.
static_traits.language_features: Expression is clear and organized, can describe specific events and emotional experiences; tone is negative, tends toward self-blame and self-deprecation; holds a skeptical attitude toward change but is willing to try (such as recording alternative self-talk).

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I am a useless wife, especially when making small mistakes (e.g., not cooking enough for my husband), which triggers inferiority and self-criticism. These feelings of inadequacy began in early pregnancy and persist to this day.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy have affected my mental health and overall well-being; I hope to address them before the baby arrives.
growth_experiences: Strong feelings of inadequacy began in early pregnancy, initially due to high stress from adjusting to pregnancy and the husband being deployed away; since then, every small slip in housework or caring for the husband develops into moments of self-doubt and self-blame.
Family and life background: living in a country house with her military husband, expecting their first child; father is a missionary; after graduating high school, mainly handling housework at home.

special_situations.event: Not enough food when cooking dinner for her husband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes in caring for my husband, it means I am a failure, a useless wife
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting unrealistic high standards, over-preparation, and self-pressure to avoid any mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even do something this simple well; I am just a useless wife; I should have done more long ago.

special_situations.event: Husband deployed away; relationship distance and uncertainty increasing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not perfect enough, I will disappoint him, proving I have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling efforts in housework and caregiving, constantly proving one's worth through actions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as I make even a small mistake, he will be disappointed, and I am a failure.

special_situations.event: Small mistakes occur in daily housework and caregiving tasks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any mistake equals overall failure, showing I am unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checks and blames self, pursuing zero errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This small mistake shows that I am a bad wife.

special_situations.event: Pregnancy bringing fluctuations in physical strength and energy, unable to maintain previous housework standards
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: No matter when, one should not make mistakes or ask for help, otherwise one is incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces oneself to endure, avoiding seeking support
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do better; if I ask for help, it proves I am not good enough.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and needed; as a wife, can show her own worth through caregiving and gain a sense of security
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing her husband, being judged incompetent, thus not being loved or being negated
defense_goal: Avoiding mistakes and external negation by maintaining perfect standards and high control
Turning harshness against the self to preempt criticism from others
Maintains hypervigilance to reduce mistakes and preserve a sense of self-worth

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, error-prone, a self that needs perfection to prove worth
object_relations.object_representation: Significant others/husband who may be disappointed and judgmental at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes viewing mistakes as learning opportunities and tries restructuring negative thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes accepting mistakes is making excuses for oneself; one must be stricter to be 'good'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using 'should/must' statements to emphasize the necessity of harsh standards, in a firm tone, refuting suggestions to relax standards with logical reasons.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to use the same compassion and tolerance toward herself as toward friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing relaxing standards will make her not good enough, so she must follow internalized external rules
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes the rule 'as a wife one should be perfect', citing others' or society's expectations as the basis, tone firm, little involvement of emotion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing everyday small mistakes and their feelings in sessions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Blames all responsibility on myself to avoid facing others' possible disappointment or criticism
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Magnifying personal faults with self-blaming language (e.g., 'It is all my fault'), minimizing external factors, in a repressed tone with a sense of guilt.

manifestations: Husband deployed away; partner separation bringing relationship distance and uncertainty
Physical and mental changes in early pregnancy adaptation and stress borne alone
Although having friends and a father to talk to, struggling to share feelings of inadequacy; subjectively feeling isolated
outcomes: Intensified self-criticism and sense of shame

manifestations: Treating the rule 'good wife = never making mistakes / always perfect' as the only right choice
Imposes self-demands of 'should / must', compressing self-choice and flexibility
outcomes: Forming unrealistic perfect standards and persistent guilt

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' self-demands (e.g., 'I should never make mistakes')
Taking 'perfect = good wife' as a self-standard without examination

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly blames self in sessions, making a big deal out of small mistakes
Skeptical about change; worries that relaxing standards will make things worse
Overly focuses on whether standards are met and ignores her own needs

positive_force: Has some social support (several close friends and father)
Invested in family roles, strong sense of responsibility
Proactively seeks psychological counseling and is willing to try new self-talk methods (such as writing down reminders)
negative_force: Overly relies on external evaluation (defines self-worth by her husband's satisfaction)
Hard to express vulnerability and seek help from the support system
Catastrophizing tendencies and marked physiological anxiety reactions

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and catastrophic automatic thoughts after small mistakes, accompanied by marked anxiety reactions (palpitations, difficulty concentrating)
antecedent: Small mistakes in housework or husband-care situations (e.g., not enough food when cooking)
Physical and energy fluctuations from pregnancy
Uncertainty and separation stress from the husband being deployed away
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner core belief that 'only perfect is good enough; otherwise one is a useless wife', with high dependence on external evaluation.
target_behavior.function: Through self-criticism, maintains high standards and a sense of control, trying to avoid disappointing others and gain confirmation of worth.
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety and tension; attention and decreased efficiency; affecting prenatal self-care and physical/mental health, and negatively impacting marital interactions.
